In the haiku, the "sapphire sea" and "graceful breach" of the humpback whale embody the fleeting moments and natural imperfections that wabi-sabi appreciates. Mono no aware, which translates to "the pathos of things," is the sensitivity to the ephemera of life. The haiku captures this through the "walnut whispers sky," suggesting a quiet, melancholic kinship between distant realms, possibly reflecting the transient nature of life and the interconnectedness of all things.
